THE CAP ON material_truth, AND THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM IN THE BUILD. What the app draws for most of 06_unfolding, and freezes into 13_messenger_states.png, is a flat beige rectangle with square corners and a hard drop shadow. That is the literal archetype docs/BRIEF.md names as a failure of the entire visual concept -- 'any procedural noise overlay, tiled repeating texture, or beige rounded rectangle standing in for paper scores this category below its floor' -- so while it ships, material_truth cannot reach 22 no matter what else is repaired, and anti_goal is charged for the same object a second time by the brief's own double-count.

FIVE OF SEVEN CRITICS NAMED THIS ONE OBJECT INDEPENDENTLY, all from the pixels: anti_goal blocking (1035x235 at x65-1099 y1281-1515, fill (253,227,200), radius 2-3px, interior std 1.35 / 168 colours / hf_mean 0.640 against 35.79 / 2182 / 6.853 for real note paper 200px below it in the same frame); material_truth blocking (a flat untextured square-cornered rectangle for at least frames 64-255 of 320, about 3.2s of the 5.33s clip, with no paper stock, no ruled lines, no tear edge, no crease and no fold seam; a 300x120 sample at (200,1350) measures mean L 230.8, L_std 1.310, HF_std 0.446 and 11 distinct luminance levels); coherence serious (std 1.4 against 52.4 for a real note body in the same screenshot); emotional_transmission (a feeling arriving as an empty box); visual_design minor (five of six sampled strip frames flat, text only in the last). It is also a stated failure condition -- 'a fold or crumple sequence playing fewer than 30 unique frames per second' -- and evidence/frames.json gives 06_unfolding repeated_fraction 0.163 with longest_still_run 23.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED, AND ONE PLAUSIBLE READING HAS ALREADY BEEN RULED OUT AT FIRING 18. logs/06_unfolding.report.json reads fold {sequence: unfold_thirds, length: 240, decoded: 13, decoding: 0, playhead: 239, held_from: 227, held_to: 239}, and it is tempting to read 'decoded: 13' as a decoder that stopped at thirteen of two hundred and forty. It is not. FoldFrames.window in app/lib/material/fold.dart:35 is 36, _held is a ROLLING window, and the report is a snapshot taken at playhead 239 -- the last frame of the sequence -- where frames 227 to 239 are the only ones left ahead. Thirteen held at the end of a 240-frame sequence is the window working correctly. All 240 PNGs are present at assets/folds/unfold_thirds/. So the report does not explain the flat rectangle and the pixels are the only evidence that does. The two candidates IMPLEMENT should separate, in this order:
  (a) DECODE CANNOT KEEP AHEAD. fold.dart:72-90 frameAt returns 'the frame at i if it is decoded, and otherwise the last one before it that is', and the comment at :77 records a past bug of exactly this shape -- 'the note sat on frame zero for the whole take and then jumped open'. If decoding falls behind, every late frame serves a stale one, which is both the held runs in frames.json and, if it falls behind from frame zero, a long flat opening. The capture took 962ms of wall clock per frame, so the decoder is being asked to keep ahead of a clock that is driven, not real.
  (b) A SEPARATE PLACEHOLDER SURFACE is drawn when nothing has decoded yet, and it is that surface -- not a fold frame -- that is measured at std 1.31. Its square 2-3px corners and uniform drop shadow do not look like any frame of a rendered fold.
Establish which before changing anything; they have different fixes and the item has five rows riding on it.

CONSTRAINT THAT MUST BE HONOURED, or closing this breaches another failure condition: 'a fold or crumple sequence ... exceeding the WebKit texture budget recorded in TASK_STATE.md'. That budget is 32 MB peak decoded per sequence; the 36-frame window peaks at 21.2 MB; the whole sequence held at once is about 141 MB. So the fix is NOT to decode the sequence. tools/check/texture_budget.py exists now and enforces this -- run it.

queue.why: The warmth half of the owner's complaint has a single upstream cause and it is not the objects. Measured this firing: every paper stock carries 3-5x more chroma in its dusk render than in its day render, off the same albedo and the same recipe -- lined_01 is Cmean 0.0132 by day and 0.0554 at dusk. That is not exposure. Darkening the day render by the same three stops the dusk rig stops down measures 0.0067, which is 0.51x, because OKLab chroma scales as the cube root of a uniform exposure change: exposure moves chroma the WRONG way, so the illuminant's hue is doing all of the work and more. The day rig's net illuminant is a near-white sun (1.0, 0.965, 0.905) at 2.6 plus a COOL sky fill (0.80, 0.83, 0.87) at 0.55, which comes to R:G:B = 1.000:0.975:0.931 -- essentially neutral. queue.worked_at_firing_22:
THE HOLE WAS REAL BUT IT WAS NOT THE ONE THIS ITEM NAMES, AND HALF THE STATED MEASUREMENT IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE. Both halves are now measured rather than argued.
WHAT WAS ALREADY SAFE. hostBind calls addressToServeOn FIRST and unconditionally, in both modes: a declared address that is not in 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 is refused, and a node with no tailnet address refuses to serve at all rather than falling back to something that happens to work. tailnet_test.dart already pinned that for the TUN branch. So the app was never one edit away from serving the conversation on a public address, which is what the brief's failure condition is protecting.
WHAT WAS NOT SAFE, AND IS THE THING WORTH HAVING FIXED. The userspace branch had NO TEST AT ALL -- and userspace is the only mode any measured run in this repository uses, because a container cannot have a TUN device, which is precisely this item's observation. The whole of that mode turned on one ternary, `boundTo = isUserspace ? '127.0.0.1' : address`, that nothing could see. Changing that literal to '0.0.0.0' would have put the conversation on every interface of the phone AND LEFT THE SUITE GREEN. Three tests now cover it: that userspace binds loopback and nothing wider while reachableAt stays a tailnet address; that a declared bad address is refused in userspace exactly as with a TUN, so userspace is not a hole shaped like the whole rule; and one property over BOTH branches at once -- the bound address is a tailnet address or loopback and nothing else, and reachableAt is always a tailnet address. RE-BROKEN: with the ternary set to '0.0.0.0', two of the three fail; restored, 167 pass and flutter analyze is clean.
WHY THE ITEM IS NOT CLOSED. Its measurement opens 'the bound address is the tailnet address in BOTH modes'. That is not implementable in userspace and no firing should try. A userspace tailscaled has no TUN, so the 100.x address is not assigned to any local interface and bind() on it fails with 'cannot assign requested address' -- it is not a policy choice that can be reversed, it is what userspace networking is. tailscaled accepts the inbound connection itself and hands it to loopback on the same port, which is why the transport's own doc comment calls loopback NARROWER than the tailnet address rather than wider. The second half of the measurement -- 'a test asserts the host refuses to bind anything outside 100.64.0.0/10 or a MagicDNS name' -- is done. ADDRESS should restate the first half as what it is actually protecting: the host binds its tailnet address where it has one, and loopback behind a userspace tailscaled, and NEVER a wildcard or a LAN address -- which is now the property the third test holds. One caveat to keep honest: loopback is reachable by any other process on the same machine, so the doc comment's 'nothing but tailscaled can reach it' is true on a phone and not true in a shared container. That is a development-mode exposure, not a shipped one.

queue.why: legibility, and it is the ruler rather than the app. A run's ground is every pixel near it that is not an ACCEPTED glyph -- `is_ground = ~dilate(glyph_px, GROUND_HALO)` at tools/check/legibility.py:507 -- and a mark is accepted only if it clears GLYPH_MIN_AREA 24, min_h 18 and the 14:1 aspect filter. Everything the app wrote that misses those filters stays in the ground and becomes the adversarial dark end the floor is taken against. Three kinds of the app's own ink do miss them, all confirmed on the committed capture by pulling the components apart in 02_chat: the two dots of a `:` are 5x5, area 18 and 21, under both the area and the height floor; digits that touch a printed rule of the stock merge into one 543x31 component and are thrown out on aspect; and a drawn rule or underline is thrown out on aspect on its own. So 'Wed 22 Apr 16:44' is failed at 1.02:1 against the ink of its own colon and its own `44`, and 'the six words' -- black ink on cream, plainly legible at 400% -- is failed at 1.14:1 against the two heavy rules the widget draws above and below it. This is the mirror image of writing-is-not-the-same-as-texture, which was the detector reading fibre as writing; this is the detector reading writing as ground.

queue.why: Found at firing 13 and it cost most of an hour before it was understood, which is the argument for it being in the queue rather than in a comment. MaterialLibrary.load() reads assets/INDEX.json off rootBundle. rootBundle is a CachingAssetBundle, so the SECOND call in a process awaits the Future the FIRST call cached -- and that Future was completed inside the first testWidgets' fake-async zone, which has since stopped. The second widget test in a file therefore never gets past its first line, and what the runner reports ten minutes later is `TimeoutException after 0:10:00`, naming no bundle, no asset and no library. Every widget test in this app needs the library, so this is a trap laid for the next person to add one, and the two that exist today only pass because one of them is first. Firing 13 guarded its own two tests with the synchronous `MaterialLibrary.loaded` getter; that is a plaster on two call sites, not a fix.
queue.measurement: Either MaterialLibrary.load() is safe to await any number of times in one process -- it memoises the decoded library itself rather than leaning on rootBundle's cache, and returns the existing instance without touching the bundle when `loaded` is true -- or it fails loudly and immediately on the second call rather than hanging. Re-break: a test file with two testWidgets, both calling `await MaterialLibrary.load()` unguarded, must pass in seconds; restore the current body and the second test must hang, which is the state today. Check the same shape for anything else reached through rootBundle: a cached bundle Future is not specific to this one function.
queue.note: FIRING 14 FIXED IT AND TOOK THE MEASUREMENT, RE-BREAK FIRST. app/test/the_library_loads_more_than_once_test.dart holds three testWidgets in one file, each calling `await MaterialLibrary.load()` with no setUpAll and no `loaded` guard -- the obvious thing, which is what the trap was laid for -- at a 30s timeout rather than the runner's ten minutes. Against the code as committed it reproduces exactly: test 1 passes in under a second, tests 2 and 3 both report `TimeoutException after 0:00:30`. With the fix all three pass in under a second. THE FIX is the first branch of this item's measurement: `load()` returns the decoded instance without touching the bundle when one exists and no explicit bundle was asked for. An explicit `bundle:` is still read, because a caller naming a bundle means 'read this one' and that is all the parameter is for; nothing in app/ or tools/ passes one today. THE SAME SHAPE ELSEWHERE, which this item also asked for, and it is clean: CachingAssetBundle caches the FUTURE of loadString and loadStructuredData and does NOT cache `load` (asset_bundle.dart:186-187 and the two overrides under them), so the trap needs a loadString. Of the three other bundle readers, MaskCache (paper.dart:30) and FoldFrames._decode (fold.dart:112) both go through `rootBundle.load` and both memoise the decoded ui.Image themselves, so neither is exposed; SeedLoader (seed_loader.dart:34) does use loadString, and is handed rootBundle from main.dart:48 and from two tests, both of which call it in setUpAll -- outside any fake-async zone -- so it is not exposed today. A widget test that called SeedLoader twice in one file would be. flutter analyze 0 errors, flutter test 119 passed.

That rule has never once executed in this build. The cost is now measured rather than hypothetical: cycle 2 to cycle 3 was +6 gross (emotional_transmission 6->10, messenger_reliability 19->20, anti_goal 5->6) against -2.5 undetected regression (material_truth 15->13, coherence 10.5->10), for the +3.5 net that reads as a thin return. queue.closed_note:
CLOSED AT FIRING 19, AND THE RE-BREAK WAS RUN. The second writer is gone: tools/capture/collect.py no longer computes SSIM, no longer writes evidence/DIFF.json, and no longer rotates evidence/.previous -- all three belonged to tools/check/diff.py, which measures before it rotates, and now only to it. The unused ssim()/label_for() helpers, the PREVIOUS constant and the shutil import went with them.
THE MEASUREMENT IS tools/check/diff_selftest.py, new, and it is end-to-end rather than a grep. A grep for writers would have passed on a build whose one writer compares a file with itself, which is the failure that actually happened, so the selftest stands up a throwaway root holding the real tools and runs capture.sh's own ordering (diff.py --rotate, then collect.py) TWICE, with one still deliberately altered upstream between the two and the other two left byte-identical. It asserts the altered still reads `changed`, the untouched ones read `unchanged`, the surviving DIFF.json is diff.py's schema (counts and baseline present), and that exactly one file in tools/ writes DIFF.json and exactly one rotates .previous. Passing run: altered still `changed` at ssim 0.9493, others `unchanged`, counts {new 0, gone 0, unchanged 2, changed 1, absent 14}.
RE-BROKEN AND WATCHED TO FAIL, as CLAUDE.md requires. With collect.py's write and rotation put back verbatim, the selftest fails five checks and the decisive line is the item's own symptom reproduced: '02_chat.png altered upstream reads None at ssim 1.0' -- a still that genuinely changed, compared with itself, reading 1.0. collect.py was then restored from the copy taken before the re-break and the selftest passes again.
AND IT NOW RUNS. No selftest in this build was invoked by anything -- not capture.sh, not run.sh, not bootstrap.sh -- which is the same shape as rank 27. diff_selftest.py is wired into capture.sh immediately BEFORE diff.py --rotate, so the ruler is checked before it is read, writing evidence/logs/diff_selftest.json and calling note_missing on failure. While wiring it, a second silent drop was found and fixed in the same file: capture.sh's note_missing entries for anything that is not one of the seventeen artifacts were read into collect.py's `reasons` and never written anywhere, so a failure reported against a derived file or a gate printed once to the console and left MANIFEST.json saying everything was fine. They are carried into manifest['missing'] now.
NOT DONE, and it is the other half of the brief's rule: the `judgement` field diff.py leaves null is still the coherence critic's to fill in, and nothing yet forces a `regressed` judgement to be acted on before the cycle continues. The comparison is now trustworthy; acting on it is a DIAGNOSE duty. The first capture after this lands will be the first in the build's history whose DIFF.json means anything, and its baseline is the firing-16 capture in evidence/.previous.

queue.closed_note: Both halves closed, at the level the measurement named. Ordering: the comparator sorted by score with the timestamp only as a tiebreak, so 4 Aug came out 07:20, 07:24, 07:14; it sorts by timestamp descending now, with the event id breaking a tie so the order is stable across runs. WHAT THE CAUSE TURNED OUT TO BE, and it is not what the item guessed. The note said to read how `offscreen` is computed and follow it; `offscreen` is computed in tools/capture/scene.js, from the crop, and is nothing to do with this. The real gap is that CaptureHooks._painted asks the framework -- paintsChild -- and the framework does not answer for a route stacked over another route: the Navigator's overlay lays its offstage entries out and declines to paint them WITHOUT overriding paintsChild to say so, exactly as RenderIndexedStack does, one level further out. THE PROOF THAT NO ROUTE FLAG FIXES IT: SearchPage has been pushed `opaque: true` since it was written, and 12_search declared the chat behind it anyway. So `opaque: true` on ViewerPage would not have closed this and was deliberately NOT changed. THE FIX: material/desk.dart now carries `OpaqueSurface`, a render object that draws nothing and says that what was painted before it is behind it, and `Desk` wraps its own stack in one -- Desk's first child is a StackFit.expand ColoredBox at full alpha in both conditions, so there is no state in which something behind shows through. CaptureHooks._collectRuns visits in paint order, and on reaching an OpaqueSurface drops every run already collected that it completely covers. Desk is what ViewerPage, SearchPage, UsRegion and the app shell are all built on, so the viewer AND the search sheet are covered by one change. A run only HALF covered is still declared, deliberately: that errs toward declaring, which costs at worst a false failure, where guessing at a partial cover would let the tool stop looking at writing that is really there. HELD BY: four cases in app/test/the_app_says_where_its_words_are_test.dart, which is where the item said the test belonged. RE-BREAK RUN: with the _hideUnder call commented out, 'writing behind an opaque surface is not declared' and 'writing on the surface is declared, and writing under it is not' both fail with the real symptom -- 'behind the desk' declared when nothing of it is on the glass -- and the half-covered case and the rest of the file still pass. queue.established_at_firing_20: ROOT CAUSE FOUND, FIXED AND MEASURED IN A LIVE BROWSER. THE firing-19 NOTE ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN IN ITS ENTIRETY: IT IS NOT THE ColoredBox FALLBACK AND IT IS NONE OF ITS THREE CANDIDATES. DO NOT SPEND A FIRING ON THEM. Each was killed by its own experiment against a real WebKit and a real build: a build with the fallback set to magenta puts NO magenta pixel anywhere in the frame, so every sheet has its render over it; removing RegionPad's RepaintBoundary (candidate c, 'the most likely') leaves the frame bit-identical; filterQuality medium->low, bit-identical; removing the pad leaves the desk at mean L 67.6, so the cream area IS the pad; and the served stock is intact at 1073x1500, L_std 25.8, whose SMOOTHEST 600x150 window is L_std 3.99 -- nine times more varied than the 0.465 the screen showed, so no part of the sheet is that smooth and the screen was not showing the sheet. THE APP WAS THEN ASKED WHAT IT HAD DRAWN, through the new __deskPaperSurfaces handle, and it answered: source 702x1500, drawn at 1.94x. Exactly one stock in the library is 702 wide -- receipt_01, a till roll: narrow, smooth, no printed rules and almost no tooth, because that is what thermal paper is, stretched across a whole phone screen. WHY THE BROWSER PICKED A TILL ROLL: hashOf is FNV-1a as `h = (h * 0x01000193) & 0xFFFFFFFF`, and a web int is an IEEE-754 double. The product reaches 3.6e16 on the first character of the first id, four times past 2^53, so it rounds and the bits it drops are the whole hash. One step of 'pad.pulse' is 4111221743 on the phone and 4111221744 in the browser. EVERY PAPER ASSIGNMENT IN THE APP DIFFERED BETWEEN THE TWO DEVICES -- stock, tear mask, which patch of the sheet shows, the tilt -- against a law DIRECTION.md states twice. On the PWA, pad.pulse and pad.chat both hashed to receipt. FIXED: the multiply is split so no intermediate leaves 2^53 and the 32-bit result is identical, so the Android build does not move and the PWA comes to meet it; and RegionPad has its own stock list without receipt or index (index_02 is 1500x933 landscape and would magnify 3.27x). MEASURED, same browser, same rect, before and after: a bare 400x200 sample goes from 4 luminance levels to 98 and L_std 0.450 to 11.274, and the frame's dominant RGB falls to 6.5%, under this item's 8% floor. The pad is ruled paper with a red margin rule down it. WHY IT IS STILL OPEN: two of four bare 400x200 samples remain under L_std 8 (5.726 and 4.238, at 49 and 47 levels, so the >= 60 clause also fails there). That is the quiet paper between a lined sheet's printed rules, magnified 2.29x. It is the SAME question as the new item no-surface-in-this-app-is-drawn-at-its-own-resolution and should be closed with it, not before it. And the committed stills are now stale in a new way: every paper assignment on the PWA has moved, so the next capture will differ from evidence/.previous almost everywhere and DIFF.json's first meaningful run will say so. That is expected and it is not a regression.

The scheduler said hasScheduledFrame=false, schedulerPhase=idle, framesEnabled=true, lifecycle=resumed, and requestAnimationFrame was frozen at 12 calls from 1.9 s to 9.8 s.
THE CAUSE. SchedulerBinding.ensureVisualUpdate schedules a frame only from `idle` and `postFrameCallbacks`; from the three phases inside a frame it returns without scheduling, on the assumption that the frame in flight will carry the change. A decode finishing during that frame's paint, or in the microtasks between its phases, is asking to repaint a subtree the frame has already painted, and the request is dropped: nothing scheduled, nothing left dirty. Any screen where something else asks for a frame afterwards recovers and nobody knows. A fresh install has no notes, no animation and nothing pending. That is why five firings on seeded screens could not see it, and why firing 20's magenta test was right and useless -- on a seeded screen the render was already cached before the widget first built, so nothing arrived late to drop.
IT WAS NOT A CAPTURE ARTIFACT. On a build with NO capture hooks compiled in, 17_setup_pwa is 47.98% one exact RGB at three seconds, eight seconds and TWENTY seconds; a pointer move, a tap and a visibilitychange all leave it. That is what a person installing the PWA saw.
AND FIRING 27'S READING WAS ONE SURFACE SHORT: 17_setup_pwa.png also carried 23.87% of exact DeskColour.day beside its sheet, because the desk's own render was dropped the same way. The first screen a new person saw was two flat fills, one on the other.
THE FIX: every place that draws a rendered surface asks for the frame -- eight Image.asset call sites through one shared frameBuilder, and MaskedLayer and NineSliced after their setState, which take the same drop through MaskCache.
MEASURED ON THE CAPTURE, not on a probe: 10_first_run 59.56% -> 0.66% with its pad-box windows 2/8 -> 6/8 and their median L_std 0.000 -> 9.200; 17_setup_pwa 47.98% -> 1.88% and 7/8 -> 8/8. Legibility on the two screens is 0 of 13 and 0 of 32. RE-BREAK by removing frameBuilder from paper.dart's stock image and watching 59.56% come back, which is the reading firing 28 took first on the committed code and which tools/check/flat_fill.py reproduces from the committed stills.
WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE: two of 10_first_run's eight windows read L_std 7.368 and 7.458 at 66 and 69 levels -- clearing the levels clause, half a point short on amplitude. That is the-paper-tooth-is-six-and-the-floor-asks-eight and it is a question about the floor.

THE DECLARATION IS OF WHAT IS PAINTED, NOT WHAT IS BUILT, and that distinction was measured rather than assumed. app.dart keeps all five regions alive in an IndexedStack, so walking every child declared 233 lines of which 127 overlapped another by more than half and 'wake me', 'quietly' and 'not at all' each appeared fourteen times -- five screens of writing laid out on top of each other, every one of them a licence to read pixels where a hidden paragraph WOULD be. A NEW QUANTITY THAT NOBODY COULD SEE BEFORE: 45 runs read against 67 lines declared. Twenty-two lines the app drew produce no reading at all, because no mark in them clears INK_DELTA or they are single short words the n<2 filter drops. routine.name: love-tap improvement loop
routine.delivery: self-bound: the Routine wakes the session that created it, and that session spawns a fresh repository-attached worker per firing with create_session
designs_that_do_not_work: Routine mints a fresh session which pushes: a minted session gets sources: [] and the proxy injects no push credential, so git push is a deterministic 403.

The minted session attaches the repository itself: it has no MCP tools. One probe told to call add_repo then push landed nothing; another told to call create_session produced no session and returned in eight seconds.

Routine wakes a named persistent orchestrator: its container had been reclaimed and the wake never re-provisioned it. Fired 22:20; the session's updated_at never moved and the Routine recorded no last_run at all.
traps_paid_for_already: list_triggers reports last_run SUCCEEDED for a firing that achieved nothing: it records delivery, not accomplishment. A commit on origin is the only proof.

update_trigger has no persistent_session_id parameter -- only create_trigger does. Passing it to update_trigger is silently ignored, so a rebinding needs the Routine recreated. Read persist_session back rather than trusting the call.
create_session cannot make a child more permissive than its parent, so a dispatcher must be created from a session that is not in plan mode or it inherits plan and stalls for ever.
routine.when_it_stops: The dispatcher is a real session with a real context window. If it fills or is archived the loop stops silently and the branch simply stops gaining commits. The fix is to create the Routine again from a new session, which is two calls; nothing is lost because loop/STATE.json holds the state.
